name: Cen Zhaoxiong
appears_on: Hurun Global (2018-2023); Hurun China (2010-2022); Hurun Self-Made Women (2018)

name: Mary Alice Malone Jr
forbes_bio: Mary Alice Dorrance Malone Jr. is a great-granddaughter of John T. Dorrance, who invented Campbell's Soup in 1897.
Mary Alice Jr. and her sister, Catherine Dorrance Malone, inherited an 18% combined stake in The Campbell's Company when their mother, Mary Alice Dorrance Malone Sr., died in June 2025.
Mary Alice Jr. replaced her mother on the company's board in July 2025. Her cousin, Bennett Dorrance Jr., and her mother's cousin, Archbold van Beuren, are also billionaire directors of the company.
Mary Alice Jr. and her sister grew up on their mother's horse breeding farm in Coatesville, Pa. An accomplished dressage rider, Mary Alice Jr. once made the U.S. Junior Olympic Equestrian Team.
She founded luxury footwear brand Malone Souliers in 2014 and relaunched the forty-year-old UK footwear brand Duo Boots in 2020 after buying the company out of bankruptcy.
Mary Alice Jr. lives in London, where she studied shoemaking at the London College of Fashion.

name: Li Zhixiong
forbes_bio: Li Zhixiong is a director of Shenzhen Longsys Electronics, a supplier of memory and storage products.
Li holds a master's degree in electronics and communication engineering from Huazhong University of Science and Technology. He did stints as in research before joining Longsys in 2004.
Lexar, a U.S. consumer storage brand acquired by Longsys in 2017, has become a global partner of the Argentina National Football Team.
Longsys went public on Shenzhen's ChiNext Market in 2022.

name: Zhang Changhong
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2011-2026)
forbes_bio: Zhang Changhong chairs DZH, formerly known as Shanghai Great Wisdom, a supplier of financial data that competes with Reuters and Bloomberg in China.

name: Christian Herz
forbes_bio: Christian Herz owns 45% of the private equity firm Mayfair SE, whose investments have included the sports apparel company Puma.
He is the grandson of Tchibo co-founder Max Herz, who built a fortune based on the importation and sale of coffee.
His father, Guenter, ran Tchibo for almost 35 years. The family also built a stake in skin-care company Beiersdorf, whose brands include Nivea.
Guenter and his sister, Daniela Herz-Schnoeckel, founded Mayfair after they were bought out of the family business in 2003.
As one of Mayfair's managing directors, Christian Herz is active in the shaping investment decisions.
forbes_facts: Italian restaurant operator Vapiano, in which Mayfair had a stake, filed for bankruptcy after all locations in several countries closed in response to the pandemic.
Daniela Herz-Schnoeckel and her children have exited Mayfair, reportedly founding Bilton Holding AG to invest primarily in real estate.

name: Paul Sciarra
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Since 2014, he has served as executive chairman of electric air taxi maker Joby Aviation. He owns a 6% stake in the company.
Sciarra held onto a roughly 5% slice of Pinterest, which went public on the New York Stock Exchange in 2019.
Since 2014, he has served as executive chairman of electric air taxi maker Joby Aviation. He owns a 6% stake in the company.
Joby went public in 2021 through a reverse merger with Reinvent Technology Partners, Mark Pincus and Reid Hoffman's SPAC.
Sciarra and his wife Jennifer signed on to the Giving Pledge in 2019, promising to donate at least half their wealth to charitable causes.
forbes_facts: Sciarra still owns 5% of Pinterest, which went public on the New York Stock Exchange in 2019.

name: André Kasprzak
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2019-2021); Hurun Global (2021)
forbes_bio: Kasprzak, along with his sister Anna and mother Hanni, owns $1.46 billion (sales) Danish shoe manufacturer, ECCO.
ECCO's products are sold in 90 countries from more than 2,200 ECCO shops and online.
ECCO was founded by Kasprzak's late grandfather, Karl Toosbuy, in 1963.
He joined ECCO's supervisory board in 2017 after his father, Dieter, stepped down as CEO.
Kasprzak previously served in the Danish military and played professional golf in the Nordic League.

name: Jean Madar
forbes_bio: Jean Madar cofounded French fragrance company Interparfums in 1982, along with Philippe Benacin.
The pair started the company out of business school after learning in class about the high margins of the fragrance industry.
They took the business public on the NASDAQ in 1988 at a $4 million valuation. It is now worth more than $3 billion.
Madar served as President of the company until 1993, when he became Director General of Interparfums' European subsidiary. He became CEO in 1997.
Madar oversees Interparfums' U.S. operations, which account for 35% of net sales.
forbes_facts: Madar never wears fragrances himself, as a way to keep his smelling palate clear.

name: Jiang Yehua
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2017-2021); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2005-2025)
forbes_bio: Jiang Yehua chairs Chongqing Huayu Group, one of the largest real estate developers in the central China city of Chongqing.
Jiang was employed as a construction worker before he set up his own business.

name: Clifford Illig
forbes_bio: Clifford Illig cofounded what became healthcare IT services company Cerner in 1979.
Illig, Neal Patterson and another colleague at consulting firm Arthur Andersen conceived the idea for Cerner while studying for a CPA exam in a park.
By 1984, they'd raised $3 million. Two years later, the founders took the company public.
Illig served as Cerner COO through 1998.
Since the 2009 HITECH law that forced U.S. hospital records to go digital Cerner's revenues have grown to $4.8 billion.
forbes_facts: He owns a stake in MLS team, Sporting Kansas City.

name: Itaru Tanimura
forbes_bio: Former McKinsey & Co consultant Itaru Tanimura founded online medical services provider M3 in 2000.
M3 listed on Tokyo's Mothers exchange for startups in 2004 and moved up to the Tokyo Stock Exchange's First Section in 2007.
The firm reported $1.3 billion in revenue in the fiscal year ended March 2020.
M3 has six million doctors using its services globally.
Electronics giant Sony has a one-third stake in M3.
